name: Lemon Herb Chicken
steps: Juice the lemons. Mince 6 cloves of the garlic. Stir the juice with that garlic, 1 tsp of the salt, the black pepper, the dried basil, and 1/4 tsp of the cayenne pepper.
Lay the chicken breasts in a deep dish and pour the lemon mixture over them. Cover and refrigerate overnight, then turn the breasts and chill 4 more hours. Leave this rest out of the timed total.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Slice the potatoes into 1/4-inch rounds and toss them with 2 tbsp of the olive oil and the remaining salt.
Lift the chicken breasts out of the dish and pat them dry. Keep the lemon mixture in the dish.
Spread the potatoes in a roasting pan and set the chicken breasts on top. Roast 25 minutes, until the skin starts to color.
Spoon the saved lemon mixture over the chicken breasts and potatoes. Roast until the thickest breast reaches 165°F (74°C) and a knife slides into the potatoes easily, about 15 to 20 minutes more.
Mince the remaining garlic. Blend it with the rest of the olive oil, the lemon juice, and the remaining cayenne pepper until the sauce is smooth and thick.
Spoon that garlic sauce over the chicken breasts and potatoes and bring the pan to the table.

attribution.note: Overnight plus morning marinade is left out of the 55 minutes. The oven is hotter than the source's 250°F hold so the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C). Green beans were not in the source and were left out. Potatoes and the garlic-oil sauce are kept. The source's cayenne dash is folded into 1/2 tsp.

name: Scrambled Eggs with Vegetables
steps: Chop the tomatoes, the cucumbers, and the onion into small pieces. Beat the eggs with the onion and 2 pinches of the salt.
Warm a wide frying pan over medium heat for 1 minute. Add the oil and tilt the pan so the surface is coated.
Add the tomatoes and the cucumbers. Cook 2 minutes, stirring now and then, until they soften at the edges. Sprinkle in the remaining salt.
Pour in the egg mixture. Cook over medium heat, turning every 30 seconds with a spatula.
Keep turning until the eggs are set into soft curds and no liquid egg remains, about 3 to 4 minutes more.
Taste a curd. If the center still looks glossy and wet, give the pan another 30 seconds over medium heat.
Divide the eggs, tomatoes, and cucumbers across four plates while they are still hot.

attribution.note: Toast is not in the source and was left out, so the name follows the scrambled eggs. Scaled from about two portions to four. Oil set to 2 tbsp because the source left it unmeasured. Salt kept as pinches and doubled with the batch.

name: Classic Cheeseburgers
steps: Trim the chuck and the sirloin and cut both into 1 1/2-inch cubes. Grind them together on a fine plate, then mix the ground meat once so the two cuts are even.
Shape four patties, each about 3/4 inch thick, and press a shallow dent in the center of each one.
Brush both sides of the patties with the olive oil and scatter the steak rub over them.
Heat a grill to high. Cook the patties about 4 to 5 minutes per side, until the center of each reaches 160°F (71°C).
In the last minute, lay one slice of pepper jack cheese on each patty and close the lid so the cheese softens.
Move the patties to a plate and rest them 3 minutes.
Split and toast the hamburger buns on the grill for about 30 seconds. Set one patty on each bottom half and close with the top.

attribution.note: Ground beef is cooked to 160°F (71°C) and rested 3 minutes. Olive oil set to 1 tbsp and steak rub to 1 tbsp because the source left both unmeasured. Unnamed toppings were left off.

name: Tomato Basil Pasta
steps: Cut the mozzarella and the tomatoes into rough cubes about the size of a sugar lump. Put both in a wide serving bowl.
Tear the basil leaves over the mozzarella and tomatoes. Pour on the olive oil, then add the salt and the black pepper. Let the bowl stand while the pasta cooks so the salt draws out juice.
Bring the water to a rolling boil in a large pot over high heat.
Add the fresh egg pasta and boil until it is tender with a little bite left, about 3 to 4 minutes for fresh noodles.
Drain the fresh egg pasta and tip it, still steaming, into the bowl of mozzarella, tomatoes, and basil.
Toss until every strand is coated and the cheese starts to soften in the heat, about 1 minute.
Serve in warm bowls while the tomatoes and mozzarella are still glossy.

attribution.sourceTitle: Cookbook:Fresh Pasta with Mozzarella, Tomato and Basil
attribution.note: Scaled from about 250 g of pasta to 500 g for four. Olive oil set to 6 tbsp, twice the source minimum of 3 tbsp. Salt set to 1 tsp and black pepper to 1/2 tsp because both were unmeasured. Water added to boil the pasta.

sources.title: Cookbook:Fresh Pasta with Mozzarella, Tomato and Basil

name: Honey Mustard Salmon
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C) and set a rack in the upper third.
Pat the salmon fillets dry. Pull out any pin bones and check that the portions are even.
Stir the honey and the coarse-grained mustard together until the glaze is even.
Spread the honey mixture over the top and underside of each salmon fillet.
Bake on the upper rack for 14 minutes.
Turn the broiler on and cook 2 minutes more, until the glaze is bubbling and the thickest fillet reaches 145°F (63°C). Pull the pan before the honey darkens.
Rest the salmon fillets 2 minutes, then move them to plates with the glaze spooned over the top.

attribution.note: Broccoli is not in the source, so the name follows Honey Mustard Salmon. Honey and mustard are set at the source's 3-to-2 ratio for four fillets. Salmon is cooked to 145°F (63°C).

name: Overnight Oats Jars
steps: Stir the rolled oats, the milk, and the chia seeds in a bowl until the seeds are scattered through the oats.
Warm the peanut butter for 10 seconds so it loosens, then swirl it through the oat mixture.
Drizzle in the honey and stir once more.
Spoon the oats into four jars, leaving a little room at the top.
Cover and refrigerate overnight, at least 8 hours, until the rolled oats are soft and the milk is absorbed. This rest sits outside the 10-minute total.
In the morning, top each jar with the mixed berries.
Eat cold, or warm a jar 45 seconds if you want the oats hot.

attribution.note: No Wikibooks page for overnight oats. Baked Oatmeal is a different dish and was not cited.

name: Turkey Taco Skillet
steps: Finely chop the onion and chop the tomato.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Add the ground turkey and the onion.
Break the ground turkey into small bits and cook until it is browned and the center of the largest piece reaches 160°F (71°C), about 8 minutes. Pour off the extra fat.
Stir in the tomato, the chili powder, the oregano, the cumin, and the black pepper.
Cook over medium heat, stirring, until the tomato softens and the spices smell toasty, about 3 minutes.
Cover, lower the heat, and simmer 15 minutes. If the ground turkey starts to stick, stir and keep the lid on so the tomato stays moist.
Uncover and cook 1 minute more so the turkey mixture is thick enough to scoop. Spoon it straight from the skillet.

attribution.note: Ground turkey is the source's beef-or-turkey choice, cooked in a skillet to 160°F (71°C). Oil set to 1 tbsp because lean turkey sticks without fat. Fresh tomato chosen instead of tomato sauce. Chili powder kept, along with the listed oregano and cumin.

name: Caprese Salad
steps: Slice each tomato into five rounds. Slice the mozzarella into pieces about the same width.
Lay the tomato slices on a platter in a single layer.
Set a slice of mozzarella on each tomato round.
Cut a short slit halfway through each stack and tuck a basil leaf into the slit so it stands up.
Sprinkle the dried oregano and the black pepper over the mozzarella and tomatoes.
Drizzle the balsamic vinegar over the platter, then drizzle the olive oil beside it so the two stay in separate ribbons.
Eat within a few minutes, while the mozzarella is still cool and the tomatoes are fresh.

attribution.note: Chicken is not in the source and was not added, so the name follows Caprese Salad. Scaled from one tomato to four. Olive oil set to 1 tbsp and black pepper to 1/2 tsp. Dried oregano set to 1 tsp. Balsamic vinegar set to 1 tbsp because it was unmeasured.

name: Black Bean Quesadillas
steps: Rinse and drain the black beans and mash them lightly so they stay in the tortillas. Warm the salsa in a small pan over low heat for 3 minutes so it is hot and not watery.
Warm the flour tortillas in a dry skillet over medium-low heat for about 20 seconds per side, until they bend without cracking. Keep them covered.
Brush the skillet with a little of the oil and set one flour tortilla in the pan.
Scatter a quarter of the Monterey Jack and cheddar over the tortilla, then spoon on a quarter of the black beans.
Cook over medium-low heat until the cheese melts and the tortilla has a few golden spots, about 2 minutes. The tortilla should not turn deep brown.
Press a second flour tortilla on top, flip the quesadilla, and cook 1 minute more until the two tortillas hold together.
Repeat with the remaining oil, tortillas, cheese, and black beans. Cut each quesadilla into wedges and spoon the salsa on the side.

attribution.note: Scaled from one quesadilla to four. Black beans kept from the filling list; other optional fillings left off. Oil set to 1 tbsp in place of unmeasured cooking spray. Salsa set to 1/2 cup.

name: Simple Italian Sausage Spaghetti Dinner
steps: Bring the water to a boil over high heat. Add the whole grain spaghetti and cook until tender with a firm center, about 9 minutes. Drain.
While the pasta cooks, peel and finely chop the onions. Mince the garlic if it is still in cloves, or measure the minced garlic.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pot over medium-high heat. Add the onions and cook 2 minutes.
Strip the casings off the Italian sausage, crumble the meat into the pot, and cook until the sausage reaches 160°F (71°C) and the onions are soft, about 6 minutes.
Pour in the dry white wine and scrape the browned bits off the bottom. Let the wine reduce by about half, 2 minutes.
Stir in the diced tomatoes with their juice, the tomato paste, the garlic, the sugar, and the dried Italian seasoning. Lower the heat to medium-low and cook 8 minutes, until the sauce is thick.
Stir in the Parmesan cheese. Toss the whole grain spaghetti with the sauce and serve in warm bowls.

attribution.note: Bell peppers are not in the source, so the name follows the sausage spaghetti. Pasta and sausage scaled up for four; the two large cans of tomatoes and the tomato paste already make enough sauce. Dry white wine chosen. Water added to boil the pasta. Sausage cooked to 160°F (71°C).

name: Greek Yogurt Parfaits
steps: Spoon a half cup of Greek yogurt into the bottom of each of four glasses.
Add a layer of granola, then a layer of mixed berries.
Repeat with the remaining Greek yogurt, granola, and mixed berries so each glass has two layers of each.
Drizzle the honey over the top of each parfait.
Let the glasses stand 2 minutes so the honey runs into the berries.
Serve at once so the granola stays crunchy against the cool Greek yogurt.
Eat them cold. The mixed berries should still look fresh and the honey should sit on top in glossy streaks.

attribution.note: No Wikibooks page for a yogurt parfait. Greek Yogurt Sauce is a sauce, not a parfait.

name: Miso Soup (Traditional)
steps: Stir the instant dashi into the water in a saucepan.
Slice the mushrooms and cube the silken tofu. Slice the scallions on a sharp diagonal.
Add the mushrooms to the dashi. Bring the pot to a bare simmer over medium heat and cook 4 minutes, until the mushrooms are tender. Do not let it boil hard.
Slide in the silken tofu and warm it 2 minutes, still at a simmer, until the cubes are hot through.
Take the pot off the heat. Ladle a little broth into a cup, whisk in the miso until smooth, and pour that back into the pot.
Stir once. Keep the miso below a boil so the flavor stays round.
Divide the soup among four bowls and top with the scallions.

attribution.note: Ginger is not in the source and was left out, so the name follows the traditional miso soup. Silken tofu, mushrooms, and scallions chosen from the garnish list and measured for four bowls. Instant dashi stirred into 6 cups of water. Miso is kept off a boil.

name: BLT Sandwich
steps: Slice the tomatoes into thin rounds and rinse the lettuce leaves.
Toast the bread until the slices are dry and golden at the edges, about 3 minutes.
Lay the bacon in a cold skillet. Set the heat to medium and cook, turning, until the strips are crisp and the fat has rendered, about 8 minutes. Drain on a plate.
Spread the mayonnaise on one side of each slice of bread.
On four slices, layer the lettuce, the tomato rounds, and the bacon. Grind or sprinkle the black pepper over the bacon.
Close each sandwich with the remaining bread, mayonnaise side in.
Cut the sandwiches in half and eat them while the bacon is still warm.
Cook until the protein reaches 165°F in the thickest part (or 145°F for fish).

attribution.note: Egg is not in the source and was not added, so the name follows BLT Sandwich. Scaled to four sandwiches. Bacon set to 12 slices because the source left it unmeasured. Mayonnaise chosen as the spread. Black pepper set to 1/2 tsp.

name: Sheet Pan Fajitas
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Cut the chicken breast into strips about 1/2 inch wide. Slice the red bell pepper, the green bell pepper, and the yellow onion into similar strips.
Toss the chicken breast with the olive oil, the ground cumin, the crushed red pepper, the salt, and the black pepper.
Spread the chicken in a single layer on a sheet pan. Roast 10 minutes.
Push the chicken to one side and add the red bell pepper, the green bell pepper, and the yellow onion. Toss everything with the juices on the pan.
Roast 12 to 15 minutes more, until the thickest piece of chicken breast reaches 165°F (74°C) and the peppers are soft with browned edges.
Let the pan rest 3 minutes so the juices settle.
Spoon the chicken, peppers, and onion onto plates straight from the sheet pan.

attribution.note: Cooked on a sheet pan instead of a skillet. Turmeric is named in the method but is not an ingredient, so it was left out. Salt set to 1 tsp and black pepper to 1/2 tsp. Tortillas are only a serving suggestion and were left out. Chicken cooked to 165°F (74°C).

name: Tuna Salad
steps: Drain the tuna and the water chestnuts. Chop the water chestnuts, the onion, and the celery. Shred the carrot.
Flake the tuna into a bowl.
Add the water chestnuts, the onion, the celery, and the carrot.
Stir in the mayonnaise, the Dijon mustard, the soy sauce, the salt, and the black pepper until the salad holds together.
Cover and chill 10 minutes so the flavors settle.
Taste and stir once more so the Dijon mustard is even.
Spoon the tuna salad onto plates. It should be cold and thick enough to mound.
Cook until the protein reaches 165°F in the thickest part (or 145°F for fish).

attribution.note: White beans are not in the source, so the name follows Tuna Salad. Used the tuna, water chestnuts, onion, celery, carrot, mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, and soy sauce. The later cheddar, grape, hot dog, and tater tot lines were left out. Salt set to 1 tsp and black pepper to 1/2 tsp. A second can of tuna brings the salad to four servings.

name: Baked Potato Bar
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Scrub the baking potatoes and dry them.
Pierce each baking potato several times with a fork so steam can escape.
Rub the cooking oil over the skins, then sprinkle on the salt.
Set the baking potatoes on the oven rack. Bake 60 minutes.
A potato is done when a skewer slides through the center with no hard spot and the skin is crisp.
Split each baking potato and fluff the inside with a fork.
Top each one with 1 tbsp of the butter and let it melt into the flesh before eating.

attribution.note: Toppings limited to butter; sour cream was the other option and was not used. Scaled from one potato to four. Salt set to 1 tsp and cooking oil to 1 tbsp because both were unmeasured. Oven method used.

name: Spaghetti and Meat Sauce
steps: Finely chop the onion, the celery, and the carrot together. Cut the bacon into small cubes. Chop the plum tomatoes.

Cook the bacon in a heavy pot over medium heat until the fat renders and the cubes are browned, about 5 minutes. Add the butter and let it melt, then stir in the onion, celery, and carrot. Cook until the vegetables are lightly browned, about 8 minutes.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Add the ground beef and break it up. Cook until it is well browned and reaches 160°F (71°C), about 8 minutes. Scrape the beef into the pot.
Pour the red wine into the skillet over high heat and scrape up the browned bits, about 1 minute. Stir in the tomato paste and the beef stock, then pour that into the pot.

Add the plum tomatoes, the bay leaf, and the lemon rind. Raise the heat until the sauce boils, then drop it so the surface only shivers. Let it cook 60 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce is thick.
Stir in the salt and the black pepper. Fish out the bay leaf and the lemon rind.
During the last 15 minutes, bring the water to a boil over high heat. Add the spaghetti and cook 10 to 12 minutes, until tender with a firm center. Drain.
Spoon the meat sauce over the spaghetti and pass the Parmesan cheese at the table.

attribution.note: Fennel left out because the source marks it optional. Bacon chosen instead of ham. Yield kept for six. Salt set to 1 tsp and black pepper to 1/2 tsp. Water added to boil the pasta. Ground beef cooked to 160°F (71°C) before the long simmer.

name: Shakshuka
steps: Mince the garlic. Dice the red bell pepper, the chile pepper, and the tomatoes.
Heat the olive oil in a wide skillet over high heat for 30 seconds. Stir in the sweet paprika and cook it in the oil for a few seconds until it smells warm.
Add the garlic, the red bell pepper, and the chile pepper. Lower the heat and cook about 10 minutes, until the peppers soften.
Add the tomatoes, the salt, and the black pepper. Bring the pan to a boil, then simmer 5 minutes until the tomatoes slump into a sauce.
Make six hollows in the sauce. Crack an egg into each hollow and spread the white a little so it meets the sauce.
Cover and cook over low heat until the egg whites are set and the yolks are still soft, about 6 to 8 minutes.
Spoon one egg and a share of the pepper sauce into each bowl.

attribution.note: Salt set to 1 tsp and black pepper to 1/2 tsp because both were unmeasured. Eggs cooked until the whites set. Yield of six eggs kept for four hungry servings.

name: Basil Pesto
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Spread the pine nuts on a small pan and toast them 8 to 10 minutes, shaking the pan once, until they are golden. They should not be dark.
Pour 2 tbsp of the olive oil into a small skillet over medium heat. Crush the garlic and cook it in that oil until soft, about 2 minutes. Pull the garlic off the heat before it browns.
Put the fresh basil, the cooked garlic, the Parmigiano-Reggiano, and the pine nuts in a blender.
With the motor running, stream in the rest of the olive oil until every drop is in the jar and the sauce turns into a thick paste.
Add the salt and the black pepper and pulse once more.
The pesto is done when the fresh basil, olive oil, Parmigiano-Reggiano, pine nuts, garlic, salt, and black pepper have turned into a smooth green paste thick enough to cling to a spoon.

attribution.note: Shown as Pesto; the Wikibooks title is Pesto I. Gnocchi is not in the source and was not added, so the dish is the pesto. Pine nuts kept. Parmigiano-Reggiano chosen. Salt set to 1 tsp and black pepper to 1/2 tsp because the source left them to taste.

name: Turkey Chili
steps: Dice the onion and the celery.
Cook the ground turkey in a large pot over medium-high heat, breaking it up, until it is browned and reaches 160°F (71°C), about 8 minutes. Pour off the fat.
Add the tomato sauce, the kidney beans with their liquid, the black beans with their liquid, and the pinto beans with their liquid.
Stir in the diced tomatoes, the water, the onion, and the celery.
Add the cumin, the chili powder, the black pepper, and the salt. Bring the pot to a boil over high heat.
Lower the heat and simmer 2 1/2 hours, stirring every 15 minutes, until the chili is thick and the beans are very soft.
If the surface looks dry near the end, stir in a splash of the remaining liquid from the pot edges and simmer 5 minutes more.
Ladle the chili into bowls once the turkey is fully tender and the sauce coats a spoon.

attribution.note: Ground turkey chosen from the source's beef, pork, or turkey. Scaled to about half for four servings, and the onion kept at one medium. Simmer kept long. Turkey reaches 160°F (71°C) before the simmer.

name: Garlic Shrimp Skillet
steps: Peel the shrimp if needed and pat them dry. Mince the garlic. Chop the parsley.
Warm the olive oil in a heavy skillet over medium heat. Add the garlic and cook about 1 minute, until it just starts to color. Do not let it blacken.
Raise the heat to high. Add the shrimp, the lemon juice, the dry sherry, and the sweet Spanish paprika.
Toss constantly until the shrimp turn pink, curl, and reach 145°F (63°C), about 3 minutes.
Take the skillet off the heat. Sprinkle on the salt and the black pepper and toss once more.
Scatter the parsley over the shrimp and the oil in the pan.
Serve from the skillet while the shrimp are still sizzling.

attribution.note: Dry sherry chosen instead of cognac. Five garlic cloves taken from the source range. Salt set to 1 tsp and black pepper to 1/2 tsp because the method seasons to taste and the ingredient list left them out. Shrimp cooked to 145°F (63°C).

name: Veggie Fried Rice
steps: Cut the carrots, the broccoli, the cabbage, and the scallions into bite-size pieces. Quarter the mushrooms and chop the onion. Mince the garlic. The cooked rice should be cold and broken up.
Heat the corn oil in a wide nonstick pan over high heat until it shimmers.
Add the onion and the garlic and stir-fry 30 seconds, until they smell sweet.
Add the carrots, the bean sprouts, the broccoli, the mushrooms, the cabbage, and the scallions. Stir-fry 3 minutes, until the broccoli is bright and the cabbage wilts.
Add the cooked rice, the salt, the light soy sauce, the vegetarian oyster sauce, and the black pepper.
Toss over high heat for 3 minutes, until the rice is hot and every grain is coated. The vegetables should be tender with a little crunch left.
Taste a grain. If the rice is still cool in the middle, cook 1 minute more, then pile it into bowls.

attribution.note: Scaled toward four servings and pack amounts converted to cups and ounces. Salt set to 1 tsp and black pepper to 1/2 tsp; the source's 2 tbsp salt and 1 tbsp pepper were far too heavy for the rice. Vegetarian oyster sauce kept. No egg was in the source.

name: Hummus
steps: The night before, stir the dried chickpeas with 2 1/2 cups of the water and the baking soda. Soak 8 hours, then drain and rinse. Leave that soak out of the timed total.
Put the chickpeas in a pot with the remaining water, the garlic, and 1 tsp of the salt. Bring to a boil over high heat.
Boil about 45 minutes, until the skins loosen. Stir and lift off as many skins as you can with a slotted spoon.
Cover and cook on low for about 2 hours, until the chickpeas collapse into a soft mass.
Drain them, keeping a few spoons of the cooking water. Mash the chickpeas through a sieve or in a food processor until smooth.
Cool 10 minutes. Beat in the tahini and enough of the saved cooking water to make a thick spread.
Chop the coriander leaves. Stir them in with the cumin and the remaining salt. The hummus is ready when it holds a soft peak and tastes savory.

attribution.note: Shown as Hummus; the Wikibooks title is Hummus I. Flatbread is not in the source and was not added, so the dish is the hummus. Overnight soak left out of the 170 minutes. Tahini set to 1/4 cup, cumin to 1 tsp, and coriander leaves to 1/4 cup because those amounts were open. A further 1/2 tsp salt is stirred in at the end.

name: Banana Pancakes
steps: Melt 40 g of the unsalted butter in a heat-safe bowl. Keep the rest for the pan.
Add the bananas and mash them into the butter until few lumps remain. Beat in the eggs until the mix looks smooth.
Stir in the whole milk a little at a time.
Whisk the self-raising flour, the ground cinnamon, the salt, and the brown sugar in a second bowl.
Pour the wet mix into the dry mix and stir until just combined. A few streaks of flour are fine.
Heat a nonstick skillet over medium heat. Grease it with a bit of the remaining unsalted butter. Pour in about 1/3 cup of batter for each pancake, leaving space between them.

Cook over medium-low heat about 3 minutes, until bubbles sit on the surface and the underside is golden. Flip and cook about 2 minutes more, until the center springs back. Repeat with the rest of the batter and butter.

attribution.note: Oats are not in the source, so the name follows Banana Pancakes. Self-raising flour chosen. An extra 15 g of unsalted butter is reserved for greasing the pan. The pinch of salt is the source amount. The batch already suits four.

name: Lemon Garlic Cod
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Pat the cod fillets dry.
Juice one lemon and slice the other into thin rounds. Mince the garlic and chop the parsley.
Stir the lemon juice, the garlic, the olive oil, the salt, and the black pepper together.
Set the cod fillets in a baking dish, pour the lemon mixture over them, and lay the lemon slices on top.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes, until the thickest fillet flakes and reaches 145°F (63°C).
Scatter the parsley over the cod.
Spoon the pan juices over each fillet and serve at once.

attribution.note: No lemon-garlic cod page. Baked Lemon Thyme Halibut and Coconut Crusted Baked Cod are different dishes.

name: Black Bean Soup
steps: Pick over the dried black beans. Cover them with 4 cups of the water and soak overnight, then drain. Leave that soak out of the timed total.
Put the beans in a pot with the remaining water. Bring to a boil, then simmer about 30 minutes, until they start to soften.
Dice the red bell pepper, the green bell pepper, and the onion. Mince the garlic and the jalapeño. Chop the cilantro.
Add each bay leaf, both peppers, the chili powder, the cumin, the garlic, the jalapeño, the onion, and the red wine vinegar.
Stir in the salt and the black pepper. Simmer 45 minutes, until the beans are fully soft and the soup has thickened.
Lift out every bay leaf. Stir in the cilantro and simmer 2 minutes more.
The soup is done when a bean mashes easily against the side of the pot. Ladle it into bowls.

attribution.note: Scaled from 6 cups of dried beans to 1 1/2 cups for four. Overnight soak left out of the 90 minutes. Water set to 8 cups for the soak and the simmer. Salt set to 1 tsp and black pepper to 1/2 tsp. Optional sour cream left off. One jalapeño chosen.

name: Herbed Caprese Salad
steps: Cut the tomatoes into thick rounds and slice the mozzarella to match.
Arrange the tomato slices on four plates.
Lay mozzarella on every tomato slice.
Rest a basil leaf on each stack.
Dust the stacks with the Italian seasoning.
Spoon the balsamic vinegar over the mozzarella, then the olive oil, keeping the two from being stirred together.
Serve right away so the tomatoes stay cool and the basil stays bright.

attribution.note: Shown as Herbed Caprese Salad; the Wikibooks title is Caprese Salad. Toast is not in the source and was not added, so this stays Caprese Salad. Scaled to four. Olive oil and balsamic vinegar each set to 1 tbsp. Italian seasoning chosen and set to 1 tsp.

name: Homestyle Lasagna
steps: Finely chop the onion, the carrots, and the celery. Mince the garlic and tear the basil.

Set a Dutch oven on the stove, pour in the olive oil, and turn the burner to medium-high. Add the ground beef and cook, breaking it up, until the liquid cooks off and the meat reaches 160°F (71°C), about 12 minutes.
Stir in the onion, the carrots, the celery, and the garlic. Cook 6 minutes, until the onion softens.
Pour in the red wine and scrape the pot. Simmer until the wine has cooked away, about 4 minutes. Add the crushed tomatoes and the sugar. Cover and simmer 20 minutes.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C). Stir the basil, the dried oregano, the salt, and the black pepper into the meat sauce.

Spread a thin layer of meat sauce in a baking dish, add a single layer of lasagne pasta sheets, then a layer of béchamel sauce. Repeat until the meat sauce is used, and finish with béchamel sauce on the top sheet.
Sprinkle the Parmesan cheese over the top. Bake on the upper rack about 45 minutes, until the cheese browns in spots and the sauce bubbles along the rim.
Rest the pan 10 minutes so the layers settle, then cut squares.

attribution.note: Onion, carrot, celery, garlic, and sugar from the ingredient list are cooked into the ragù. Ground beef reaches 160°F (71°C). Béchamel is used as the listed sauce. Yield kept for eight. Baked until bubbling.

name: Herbed Tomato Soup
steps: Dice the onion if it is not already diced. Slice the basil leaves into thin strips and set them aside. Measure the basil and the thyme.
Heat the olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until it is tender but not browned, about 5 minutes.
Add the diced tomatoes, the vegetable broth, the tomato sauce, the basil, the thyme, and the black pepper.
Bring the pot to a boil over high heat.
Lower the heat, cover, and simmer 20 minutes, until the onion disappears into the soup and the broth tastes sweet.
Stir in the balsamic vinegar off the heat.
Ladle into bowls and scatter the basil leaves on top. Leave the soup chunky.

attribution.note: Vegetable broth chosen instead of chicken broth. The soup is simmered and ladled, not blended, so the name follows Herbed Tomato Soup. Optional balsamic vinegar and basil-leaf garnish kept. Black pepper kept as 1 dash.

name: Greek Chicken Wrap
steps: The cooked chicken should already have reached 165°F (74°C) when it was first cooked. Shred it if the pieces are large. Chop the fresh oregano.
Stir the feta cheese, the cooked chicken, the Greek yogurt sauce, and most of the fresh oregano in a bowl. Save a little oregano for the top.
Brush one side of each flour tortilla with the olive oil.
Spoon a quarter of the chicken mixture along the middle of each flour tortilla.
Fold in the sides and roll the tortilla so the filling stays inside.
Set the wraps seam side down. They are meant to be eaten cold, so do not toast them.
Sprinkle the remaining fresh oregano over the wraps and cut them in half.

attribution.note: Pita is not in the source, so the name follows Greek Chicken Wrap. Olive oil set to 1 tbsp because it was unmeasured. Chicken is used already cooked, with a 165°F (74°C) cue for that earlier cooking.

name: Sweet Potato Hash
steps: Peel the sweet potatoes and cut them into 1/2-inch cubes. Dice the onion and the bell pepper. Mince the garlic.
Heat the olive oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers.
Add the sweet potatoes in one layer. Cook 8 minutes, stirring every couple of minutes, until the edges brown.
Add the onion and the bell pepper. Cook 6 minutes, until the onion is soft and the sweet potatoes are tender in the center.
Stir in the garlic, the paprika, the salt, and the black pepper. Cook 1 minute, until the garlic smells sweet and the paprika coats the pan.
The hash is done when a cube of sweet potato mashes with a fork and the vegetables have browned spots.
Spoon the hash onto plates straight from the skillet.

attribution.note: No sweet-potato hash page. Hash Browns and Baked Sweet Potatoes are different dishes.

name: Vegetarian Soft Tacos
steps: Chop the tomato and shred the lettuce. Split the onion into two cups: one for the pan and one for the table. Mince the garlic.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-low heat. Add 1 cup of the onion and cook until it softens, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, the chilli powder, the paprika, the salt, and the red pepper. Cook 1 minute.
Add the ground beef substitute and the water. Cook 10 to 12 minutes so the water nearly cooks off and the crumbles are hot through.
Warm the refried beans in a small pot over low heat, stirring, until they are steaming, about 5 minutes.
Heat a second pan over medium-low heat. Warm each flour tortilla about 30 seconds per side, until flexible and spotted.
Set out the remaining onion, the tomato, the lettuce, the Colby-Jack cheese, and the sour cream. Fill the tortillas with the crumbles and the refried beans and add the toppings at the table.
Cook until the protein reaches 165°F in the thickest part (or 145°F for fish).

attribution.note: Lentils are not in the source, so the name follows Vegetarian Soft Tacos. Oil set to 1 tbsp so the onions can brown. Sour cream set to 1/2 cup because it was unmeasured. Both cups of onion from the source are used, one cooked and one raw.

name: Simple Chicken Salad
steps: The cooked chicken should have reached 165°F (74°C) when it was first cooked. Dice it. Chop the lettuce and mince the garlic.
Set a skillet over medium heat. Cook the bacon until it is crisp, about 6 minutes, then drain and dice it.
Stir the mayonnaise, the dressing, and the garlic in a bowl.
Add the cooked chicken, the bacon, and the lettuce.
Toss until every piece is coated and the salad looks even.
Chill 5 minutes, or serve at cool room temperature.
The salad is ready when the lettuce is still crisp and the chicken is cold. Spoon it onto plates.

attribution.note: Cucumber is not in the source, so the name follows Simple Chicken Salad. Mayonnaise set to 1/4 cup, lettuce to 2 cups, and bacon to 4 slices because those amounts were open. Dressing kept at 1 tsp and garlic at 1 tsp.

name: Mushroom Omelette
steps: Slice the mushrooms and the fennel. Mince the garlic. Beat the eggs and the egg whites together until the yolks and whites are one color.
Heat 1 tsp of the oil in a small skillet over medium heat. Add the mushrooms, the fennel, and the garlic.
Cook about 4 minutes, until the mushrooms give up their liquid and the fennel is tender. Scrape the filling onto a plate.
Add 1 tsp of the oil to the same skillet over medium heat. Pour in half the eggs and half the egg whites.
Cook, lifting the edges so uncooked egg runs under, until the top is just set, about 2 minutes. The center should not be liquid.
Add half the mushroom filling, fold the omelette, and slide it onto a plate. Repeat with the last of the oil, the remaining eggs, the remaining egg whites, and the rest of the filling.
Each omelette is done when the outside is golden in spots and the egg white is fully set.

attribution.note: Mushrooms kept, with the garlic and fennel from that same filling line. Other fillings left off. Oil set to 1 tbsp. Mushrooms set to 4 oz and fennel to 1 small bulb. Doubled for two omelettes. No milk was in the ingredient list.

name: Sesame Noodle Salad
steps: Chop the cilantro and the scallions. Slice the carrots into thin matchsticks.
Bring the water to a boil over high heat. Add the angel hair pasta and cook until tender, about 3 minutes. Drain well.
Toss the hot angel hair pasta with the sesame oil, the olive oil, and the salt.
Add the cilantro, the scallions, and the carrots and toss until the noodles are coated.
Spread the salad in a shallow dish so it cools quickly.
Chill at least 10 minutes, until the noodles are cool and the carrots are still crisp.
Toss once more and serve cold.

attribution.note: Ginger is not in the source, so the name follows Sesame Noodle Salad. Scaled to about half for four. Olive oil set to 1 tbsp for the optional splash. Water added to boil the pasta. Salt halved with the batch to 1 1/2 tsp.

name: Italian White Bean Soup
steps: Soak the dried white beans in plenty of cold water for 12 hours, then drain. Leave that soak out of the timed total. Cut the carrot, the onion, and the leeks into chunks. Cut the celery into short lengths.
Put the beans in a pot with the salt, the butter, the carrot, the onion, the leeks, the celery, and the water.
Simmer over low heat about 70 minutes, until the beans are very soft and the vegetables are falling apart.
Drain the pot. Discard the carrot, the onion, the leeks, and the celery. Puree the beans, adding the chicken stock until the puree is smooth.
Return the puree to the pot, bring it to a gentle boil, and keep it hot.
Whisk the egg yolks with the cream. Stir that into the hot soup off the boil so the yolks thicken it without scrambling. Cook over low heat 2 minutes, stirring, until the soup coats a spoon.
Cook until the protein reaches 165°F in the thickest part (or 145°F for fish).
Boil the peas 3 minutes until they are bright, then stir them into the soup. Serve with the croutons on the side.

attribution.note: Name set to Italian White Bean Soup. Chicken stock chosen instead of veal. Scaled to 8 oz of dried beans for four. Salt set to 1 tsp and butter to 2 tbsp because both were unmeasured. Extra water is used for the soak and drained; 4 cups go into the simmer, plus 2 cups chicken stock. Egg yolks set to 2. Peas set to 1 cup and croutons to 1 cup. Overnight soak left out of the 90 minutes.

name: Ribeye Stir-Fry
steps: Slice the ribeye steak thinly across the grain. Season the slices with the salt and the black pepper. Mince the Thai bird chilis and the garlic. Dice the onions, julienne the carrot, and cut the scallions into thin strips. Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 minutes, until they smell nutty.
Film a wok with the peanut oil and heat it over medium-high heat. Add the onions and the garlic. Stir until the garlic is golden, about 1 minute. Scoop them out.

Add the ribeye steak in two batches. Stir-fry each batch about 1 minute, until the slices are browned and the center of a thick piece reads 145°F (63°C) for medium. Move them to a plate and rest 3 minutes.
Add the Thai bird chilis, the carrot, the soy sauce, the honey, the rice wine vinegar, and the scallions to the wok.
Stir-fry over high heat about 2 minutes, until the carrot is lightly browned at the edges and the honey is bubbling.
Return the onions, the garlic, and the rested ribeye steak to the wok. Toss about 30 seconds, until everything is hot.
Sprinkle the sesame seeds over the stir-fry and serve at once.

attribution.note: Shown as Ribeye Stir-Fry because the page uses ribeye steak rather than a generic beef label. Broccoli is not in the source, so the name follows Beef Stir-Fry. Scaled about threefold for four. Peanut oil set to 2 tbsp, salt to 1 tsp, and black pepper to 1/2 tsp. Steak cooked to medium and rested 3 minutes.

name: Shakshuka for Two
steps: Peel and chop the yellow onion. Chop the plum tomatoes and the bell pepper.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the yellow onion and cook until it turns translucent, about 6 minutes.
Add the plum tomatoes and the bell pepper.
Stir in the dried basil, the cayenne pepper, the paprika, and the turmeric. Cover and cook on low about 25 minutes, until the tomatoes are soft all the way through and the sauce is thick.
Make two hollows in the onion and tomato mix. Crack one egg into each hollow.
Cover and cook on low about 5 minutes more, until the egg whites are firm and the yolks are set at the edges.
Spoon an egg and a share of the pepper sauce into each of two bowls.

attribution.note: The source already uses two eggs, so the batch was kept for two. Dried basil chosen instead of black pepper. Cayenne pepper set to 1/4 tsp, paprika to 1 tsp, and turmeric to 1/2 tsp because those were to taste. Bread is only a serving suggestion and was left out.

name: Peruvian Lime Chicken
steps: Juice the limes. Mince the garlic. Stir the juice with the garlic, the cumin, the paprika, the dried oregano, the salt, the black pepper, and the olive oil.
Coat the chicken thighs with that mixture. Cover and chill at least 30 minutes. Leave the chill out of the 45 minutes.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Lift the chicken thighs onto a sheet pan and pour the marinade over them.
Roast 35 minutes, until the skin is browned and the thickest thigh reaches 165°F (74°C).
If the chicken thighs still look pink at the bone, roast 5 minutes more and check 165°F (74°C) again.
Rest the chicken thighs 5 minutes.
Spoon the pan juices over the thighs and serve.

attribution.note: No pollo a la brasa or Peruvian lime-chicken page. Ají de Gallina is a different dish.

name: Tadka Dal
steps: Chop the onions as fine as you can. Chop the chilli, the garlic, the ginger, and the fresh chilli.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the onions and cook 8 minutes, until they soften and turn pale gold.
Add the chilli, the garlic, and the ginger. Cook 1 minute.
Stir in the split red lentils, the chopped tomatoes, the vegetable stock cube, the water, and the cardamom pods.
Add the garam masala, the paprika, the black pepper, the mustard seed, and the fresh chilli.
Cover and simmer over low heat about 25 minutes, stirring once or twice, until the split red lentils are soft and the curry is thick.
Fish out the cardamom pods if you see them. The dhal is done when a spoon stands up in the pot and the onions have melted into the sauce.

attribution.note: Shown as Tadka Dal; the Wikibooks title is Tadka Dhal (Spiced Lentil Curry) I. Coconut milk is not in the source, so the name follows the spiced lentil curry. Oil set to 1 tbsp so the onions can soften. Water set to 2 cups. Black pepper set to 1/2 tsp. A vegetable stock cube is used because the cube type was not named. Both chillies kept.

name: Bulgogi
steps: Slice the beef as thin as you can. Slice the green onions on a diagonal, slice the button mushrooms, and slice the onion thinly.
Stir the beef with the green onions, the button mushrooms, the onion, the soy sauce, the sugar, the sesame oil, the black pepper, the garlic, and the mirin.
Cover and marinate 30 minutes. Leave that rest out of the 25 minutes.
Heat a grill to high. Lift the beef out of the marinade and lay the slices on the grate.
Grill about 1 minute per side for medium, until the edges brown and the center is hot, about 145°F (63°C).
Rest the beef 3 minutes. While it rests, set the onion and button mushrooms on the grill for 2 minutes so they soften.
Toss the beef with the grilled onion, the button mushrooms, and the green onions from the bowl, and serve.

attribution.note: Lettuce is not in the source, so the name follows Bulgogi. Optional mushrooms, onion, and mirin kept. Pepper kept at the source's 4 tsp. Marinade left out of the timed total. Beef cooked to medium and rested 3 minutes. Rice was only a serving suggestion and was left out.

name: Moroccan Chickpea Stew
steps: Chop the onion, the zucchini, the green bell pepper, and the chile pepper. Mince the garlic. Chop the cilantro.
Put the onion and the vegetable broth in a pot over medium heat. Cook about 8 minutes, until the onion softens.
Add the zucchini, the canned tomatoes, the green bell pepper, the chile pepper, and the garlic. Cook 12 minutes, until the zucchini and peppers are soft.
Stir in the cooked chickpeas, the peanut butter, the coriander, the turmeric, the cumin, the salt, and the black pepper.
Simmer 8 minutes, until the peanut butter dissolves and the stew is thick.
The chickpeas should be hot through and the sauce should coat them.
Sprinkle the cilantro on top and serve in bowls.

attribution.note: Cooked chickpeas chosen so no overnight soak is needed. Soy sauce left out in favor of the listed salt, which keeps the stew gluten-free. Rice is mentioned in the method but is not an ingredient, so it was left out. Cilantro garnish kept. Yield suits four.

name: Caprese Salad for Two
steps: Slice the tomatoes into rounds and slice the mozzarella to the same thickness.
Overlap the tomato slices and the mozzarella on two plates.
Tuck a basil leaf between each tomato and mozzarella slice.
Sprinkle the dried oregano and the black pepper over both plates.
Drizzle the balsamic vinegar in a thin line, then the olive oil in a second line.
Do not toss the plates. The dressing should sit on the surface.
Eat at once, while the mozzarella is cool and the basil is fragrant.

attribution.note: Shown as Caprese Salad for Two; the Wikibooks title is Caprese Salad. Bread is not in the source, so this is Caprese Salad for two rather than a pressed sandwich. Scaled from one tomato to two. Olive oil set to 1 tbsp and black pepper to 1/2 tsp. Dried oregano set to 1/2 tsp. Balsamic vinegar set to 1 tbsp.

name: Pad Kra Pao Gai (Thai Basil Chicken Stir Fry)
steps: Slice the Thai chillies and chop the garlic. Chop the green beans into short pieces. Tear the Thai basil if the leaves are large.
Heat the cooking oil in a wok over high heat until it shimmers, about 1 minute.
Add the Thai chillies and the garlic. Stir-fry about 15 seconds, until they smell sharp.
Add the minced chicken. Stir-fry, breaking up clumps, until the chicken is no longer pink and the thickest bits reach 165°F (74°C), about 4 minutes.
Add the green beans. Stir-fry 1 minute.
Pour in the fish sauce and the oyster sauce and add the sugar. Stir-fry 2 minutes, until the green beans are tender-crisp and the sauce coats the chicken.
Turn the heat off, add the Thai basil, and stir about 10 seconds, until the leaves wilt. Serve from the wok.

attribution.sourceTitle: Cookbook:Pad Kra Pao Gai (Thai Basil Chicken Stir Fry)
attribution.note: Pork is not in the source. Minced chicken is kept and cooked to 165°F (74°C). Rice and a fried egg are serving suggestions, not ingredients, so they were left out. Six Thai chillies and 16 basil leaves taken from the source ranges.

sources.title: Cookbook:Pad Kra Pao Gai (Thai Basil Chicken Stir Fry)

name: Greek Lemon Orzo
steps: Chop the parsley and the kalamata olives. Cut the sundried tomatoes into strips. Drain the pickled capers. Crumble the feta cheese.
Bring the water and the ground turmeric to a boil in a large pot over high heat.
Stir in the orzo and boil until it is tender with a little bite, about 8 minutes. Drain and rinse briefly with cold water.
Shake the pickled capers, the lemon juice, the olive oil, the salt, the black pepper, and the sugar in a jar until the dressing looks cloudy and even.
Pour that dressing over the orzo and toss until the pasta is coated and tinted from the turmeric.
Add the parsley, the sundried tomatoes, the kalamata olives, and the feta cheese. Toss again.
Serve warm or at room temperature, while the orzo is still glossy.

attribution.note: Scaled to about half for four. Water added to boil the orzo. Lemon juice, olives, and feta kept, so the Greek lemon character stays. Amounts of salt, pepper, and sugar halved with the batch.

name: Breakfast Burritos
steps: Warm the bacon in a skillet over medium heat until the slices are hot and the edges crisp again, about 3 minutes. The bacon is already cooked.
Beat the eggs with the salt and the black pepper. Scramble them in the same skillet over medium-low heat, stirring, until the curds are set and no liquid egg remains, about 4 minutes.
Heat the hash browns in a nonstick pan over medium-high heat until they are browned and hot through, about 8 minutes.
Warm the flour tortillas in a dry skillet about 20 seconds per side so they bend without cracking.
Warm the hollandaise sauce over low heat, stirring, for 2 minutes. Grate or slice the cheese if it is in a block.
On each flour tortilla, layer a cup of hash browns, two slices of bacon, two eggs, a quarter of the cheese, and a spoon of hollandaise sauce.
Roll each tortilla tightly so the filling stays inside. The eggs should be fully set before the burritos are closed.
Cook until the protein reaches 165°F in the thickest part (or 145°F for fish).

attribution.note: Bacon chosen instead of breakfast sausage. Hash browns set to 4 cups, hollandaise sauce to 1/2 cup, and cheese to 4 oz because those amounts were open. Salt set to 1 tsp and black pepper to 1/2 tsp. Eggs scrambled until set.

name: Cincinnati-Style Chili
steps: Finely chop the onions and mince the garlic. Crumble the raw ground beef into a pot of the cold water.
Add the tomato paste, the onions, the garlic, the vinegar, and the Worcestershire sauce.
Add the chili powder, the salt, the cumin, the oregano, the cayenne pepper, the black pepper, the cinnamon, the allspice, the marjoram, the ground cloves, and the bay leaves.
Stir and break the ground beef apart before any heat goes on, so the crumbles stay small.
Cover and simmer over low heat for 2 hours, stirring now and then, until the chili is thick and the beef reaches 160°F (71°C).
Cool the pot, then refrigerate until the fat firms on top, about 30 minutes. Lift off the fat and discard each bay leaf.
Reheat over medium heat until the chili is steaming, about 10 minutes, and ladle it into bowls.

attribution.note: Name set to Cincinnati-Style Chili. The source batch is kept for six. Ground beef reaches 160°F (71°C). The chill used to lift the fat is included in the 180 minutes.

name: Miso Butter Cod
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Pat the cod fillets dry.
Stir the white miso, the butter, the mirin, and the sugar into a paste. Slice the scallions.
Spread the miso paste over the top of each cod fillet.
Set the fillets in a small baking dish. Bake 12 minutes.
The cod is done when it flakes and the thickest fillet reaches 145°F (63°C). The miso top should look glossy and a little browned.
If the center is still translucent, bake 3 minutes more and check again.
Scatter the scallions over the cod and serve with the pan juices.

attribution.note: No miso-butter cod page.

name: Vietnamese Lemongrass Tofu
steps: Press the firm tofu for 10 minutes, then cut it into 1-inch cubes. Pat the cubes dry.
Trim the lemongrass and mince the tender cores. Mince the garlic.
Stir the lemongrass, the soy sauce, the maple syrup, the garlic, the chili paste, and the lime juice into a glaze.
Heat the vegetable oil in a skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers.
Add the firm tofu in one layer. Cook about 3 minutes per side, until the faces are golden.
Pour in the lemongrass glaze. Toss over medium heat 2 minutes, until the glaze bubbles and coats every cube and the tofu is hot in the center.
The dish is done when the tofu is browned and the sauce is sticky. Spoon it into bowls.

attribution.note: No lemongrass tofu page. Tofu in Spiced Coconut Sauce is a different dish.

name: Garlic Shrimp with Lemon Butter Sauce
steps: Peel and devein the shrimp. Season them with the salt and the black pepper. Mince the garlic and the shallot. Juice the lemon.
Melt 2 tbsp of the unsalted butter with the olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the garlic and cook, stirring, until it turns gold, about 1 minute.
Add the shrimp and cook, tossing, until they are pink, opaque, and reach 145°F (63°C), about 3 minutes. Move them to a warm plate.
In a saucepan over medium heat, melt 2 tbsp more of the unsalted butter. Add the shallot and cook 30 seconds.
Add the lemon juice, the heavy cream, and the rest of the unsalted butter. Cook 2 minutes, until the butter melts and the sauce is hot and smooth.
Spoon the lemon sauce over the shrimp and serve while both are warm.

attribution.sourceTitle: Cookbook:Garlic Shrimp with Lemon Butter Sauce
attribution.note: Name follows Garlic Shrimp with Lemon Butter Sauce. Scaled to about half for two, with one small shallot and 2 tbsp heavy cream standing in for a splash. Salt set to 1 tsp and black pepper to 1/2 tsp because both were unmeasured. Shrimp cooked to 145°F (63°C).

sources.title: Cookbook:Garlic Shrimp with Lemon Butter Sauce

name: BBQ Baby Back Ribs
steps: Crack the black peppercorns. Stir 1/4 cup of the dark brown sugar with the chili powder, the garlic powder, the cayenne pepper, the salt, the black peppercorns, and the smoked paprika. Rub that all over the meat side of the baby back pork ribs. Refrigerate at least 1 hour. Leave that rest out of the timed total.

Put the tomato paste, the molasses, the remaining dark brown sugar, and the apple cider vinegar in a saucepan. Bring to a boil over high heat and cook until the sauce is reduced by about half, 15 to 20 minutes. Set it aside.
Scatter the hickory wood chips and the applewood chips in a roasting pan. Set a rack over them and lay the baby back pork ribs on the rack.
Cover the pan tightly and cook in a 200°F (93°C) oven for 6 hours, brushing with the sauce every hour.
The ribs are ready to finish when the meat is fork-tender and the internal temperature is well above 145°F (63°C).
Heat the broiler. Brush the meat side with more sauce and broil until the surface is well browned, about 4 minutes. Watch so the sugar does not burn.
Rest 5 minutes, slice into single ribs, and serve warm with the remaining sauce.

attribution.note: Oven method used, with smoked paprika and wood chips in the pan. The one-hour rub rest is left out of the 390 minutes. Ribs are cooked until fork-tender and past 145°F (63°C). Sauce amounts follow the source.

name: Jamaican Jerk Chicken Skewers
steps: Cut the chicken breasts into 1 1/2-inch chunks and thread them onto skewers.
Stir the dark rum and the brown mustard together and rub that over the chicken.

Mix the ground allspice, the salt, the black pepper, the cayenne pepper, the ground ginger, the ground cinnamon, the nutmeg, the dried thyme, and the dehydrated lemon peel. Rub that spice mix over the chicken.
Refrigerate at least 1 hour. Leave that marinade out of the 30 minutes.
Heat a grill to medium-high and oil the grate. Cook the skewers, turning often, until the thickest chunk of chicken breast reaches 165°F (74°C), about 12 to 15 minutes.
Rest the skewers 10 minutes.
The chicken should be opaque at the center and browned at the edges before it is eaten.

attribution.note: Chicken breasts cut for skewers. Marinade left out of the timed total. Chicken cooked to 165°F (74°C). Onion is not in the source and was left out.

name: Kyopulo (Eggplant with Peppers and Tomatoes)
steps: Heat a grill pan or the broiler to high. Prick the aubergines and the bell peppers.
Roast the aubergines and the bell peppers, turning every few minutes, until the skins blacken and the flesh collapses, about 20 minutes.
Cover them 10 minutes, then peel off the skins and chop the flesh into small pieces.
Dice the tomatoes and crush the garlic. Chop the parsley.
Stir the tomatoes into the aubergines and bell peppers, then stir in the garlic.
Add the sunflower oil, the vinegar, and the salt. Beat the mixture hard with a wooden spoon until it looks glossy and even.
Spread it on a plate and top with the parsley. It is ready when the vegetables are soft and the vinegar tastes bright, not raw.

attribution.note: Name follows Kyopulo. The vegetables are roasted on high heat, as the source does, then mixed rather than baked as a casserole. Sunflower oil set to 1 tbsp, vinegar to 1 tbsp, and salt to 1 tsp because all three were unmeasured. Parsley set to 1/4 cup. Three eggplants and four bell peppers taken from the source ranges.

name: Sichuan Mapo Tofu
steps: Slice the onion and the mushrooms. Mince the garlic. Cut the green onions into 1-inch pieces. Cube the silken tofu. Toast the Sichuan pepper in a dry pan over medium heat for 1 minute, then grind it.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Add the onion, the ginger, and the dried chile pepper and cook 2 minutes, until the onion softens.
Add the minced beef and the garlic. Fry until the beef is browned and reaches 160°F (71°C), about 4 minutes.
Stir in the chili bean paste, the Sichuan pepper, the soy sauce, the rice wine, and the mushrooms.
Slide in the silken tofu and the green onions. Lower the heat and simmer 8 minutes, until the tofu is hot and the sauce is glossy and thick.
Stir gently so the tofu cubes stay mostly whole.
The mapo is done when the beef is fully cooked and the sauce clings to the tofu. Spoon it into bowls.

attribution.note: Minced beef chosen instead of pork. Oil set to 1 tbsp because the sauté needs fat. Optional mushrooms kept. Rice is only a serving suggestion and was left out. Beef cooked to 160°F (71°C).

name: Brazilian Black Bean Soup
steps: Cover the dried black beans with 2 cups of the water. Bring to a boil, then take the pot off the heat, cover, and let stand 1 hour. Drain.
Mince the garlic and dice the white onion. Chop the green onion. Juice half the lime and cut the rest into wedges. Tie the clove in a small piece of cloth if you want to lift them out later.
Return the beans to the pot with the remaining water, the garlic, the salt, the white onion, the cumin, the ground hot pepper, the black pepper, and the lime juice.
Add the clove. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 2 hours.
The soup is ready when the beans are tender and the liquid is thick. Mash a few beans against the side of the pot if you want it richer.
Stir in the green onion and simmer 2 minutes more. Remove the clove.
Ladle into bowls and serve with the lime wedges.

attribution.note: Dried black beans kept. Scaled to about half for four: 1 cup beans and 6 cups water. Salt set to 1 tsp and black pepper to 1/2 tsp. The one-hour stand and both simmer stretches are inside the 300 minutes.

name: French Omelette
steps: Beat the eggs just until the yolks and whites blend. Stir in the salt and the black pepper.
Set a frying pan over high heat. When it is hot, add the oil and the butter and swirl until the butter melts and both fats coat the pan.
Let the pan get very hot without letting the butter turn dark.
Pour in the eggs and tilt so they cover the bottom.
With a spatula, pull the set edges toward the center and tilt so liquid egg fills the gap. Repeat for about 45 seconds, until the top is still barely wet and the bottom is set.
Lower the heat. Loosen the omelette, fold it in half, and cook 15 seconds more so the fold sets.
Slide it onto a plate. The outside should be yellow and tender, not browned, and the eggs fully cooked at the fold.

attribution.note: Herbs are not in the source, so the name follows French Omelette. Salt set to 1 tsp, black pepper to 1/2 tsp, oil to 1 tbsp, and butter to 1 tbsp because all were unmeasured. Four eggs kept for two.

name: Caribbean Coconut Rice & Peas
steps: Rinse the dried kidney beans. Put them in a pot with the water, the salt, and the crushed garlic. Soak overnight, then leave that soak out of the 50 minutes.
Set the covered pot over medium heat until the liquid boils. Keep a gentle bubble, stirring now and then, until the dried kidney beans are tender, about 20 minutes.
Chop the scallions. Lower the heat and add the coconut milk, the whole Scotch bonnet pepper, the scallions, the thyme, the margarine, the all-purpose seasoning, and the seasoning salt.
Cover and boil gently 10 minutes. The Scotch bonnet pepper should stay whole so it perfumes the pot without bursting.
Stir in the white rice, cover, and lower the heat. Cook 15 minutes, until the rice is soft and the liquid is absorbed.
Remove the Scotch bonnet pepper and the garlic clove if it is still whole.
Fluff the rice and beans. They are done when the grains are tender and separate and the beans are soft.

attribution.note: Kidney beans chosen instead of pigeon peas, and white rice instead of brown. Scaled to about one third for four. Overnight soak left out of the 50 minutes. Optional chicken seasoning left out so the dish stays meat-free. Coconut milk set to 3/4 cup with the scale.

name: Lebanese Fattoush Salad
steps: Mince the garlic. Tear the romaine lettuce. Dice the cucumber and the tomato. Chop the green onions, the parsley, the mint, the green bell pepper, and the purslane.
Put the water and the cornstarch in a little pan. Cook over medium-high, stirring, for about 2 minutes, until the mixture thickens.
Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the lemon juice, the garlic, the sumac, the salt, and the black pepper. Cool the dressing while you cut the vegetables.
Toast the pita until dry and spotted, about 4 minutes, then tear it into pieces.
Toss the romaine lettuce, the cucumber, the tomato, the green onions, the parsley, the mint, the green bell pepper, the purslane, and the arugula in a large bowl.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss until the leaves look lightly coated.
Add the pita and serve at once so the bread stays a little crisp.

attribution.note: Scaled to about half for four. Salt set to 1 tsp and black pepper to 1/2 tsp. The cornstarch dressing is cooked as the source does, then chilled only for the few minutes of chopping.

name: Sweet Italian Sausage Skillet
steps: Bring the water to a boil over high heat. Add the rotini and cook until tender, about 8 minutes. Drain.
Slice the sweet Italian sausage into rounds. Heat the cooking oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Brown the sausage about 5 minutes, until the centers reach 160°F (71°C). Pour off the extra fat.
Stir in the stewed tomatoes with their juice, the tomato paste, the chicken broth, and the drained Italian green beans.
Bring the skillet to a boil, then lower the heat, cover, and simmer 10 minutes, until the beans are hot and the sauce is thick.
Stir in the rotini and cook 1 minute so the pasta takes up the sauce.
Sprinkle the provolone over the top, cover 1 minute until it melts, and serve from the skillet.

attribution.note: Bell peppers are not in the source, so the name follows Sweet Italian Sausage Skillet. Provolone chosen instead of mozzarella. Water added to boil the pasta. Sausage cooked to 160°F (71°C). Yield kept for four.

name: Japanese Teriyaki Salmon
steps: Stem the Thai bird chiles. Blend the soy sauce, the ginger, the garlic, the rice wine vinegar, the lemon zest, the light brown sugar, and the Thai bird chiles until the marinade is smooth.
Put the salmon fillets in the marinade, turn them to coat, and refrigerate up to 4 hours. Leave that rest out of the 25 minutes.
Lift the salmon out and pat it dry. Brush every side with the sesame oil.
Heat a grill to high. Lay the salmon skin side up over the hottest area.
Cook 4 minutes, then turn and cook 3 to 4 minutes more, until the thickest fillet reaches 145°F (63°C) for a moist center.
Move the fillets to a plate, cover, and rest 5 minutes.
Serve with any glaze left on the plate. The flesh should flake and look just opaque.

attribution.note: Sesame oil set to 1 tbsp because it was unmeasured. Marinade left out of the timed total. Salmon cooked to 145°F (63°C) and rested.

name: Indian Saag Paneer
steps: Cube the paneer. Chop the onion, the tomato, and the green chili. Mince the garlic and the ginger. Wash the spinach.
Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the paneer on two sides, about 2 minutes per side, until golden. Set it aside.
Add the remaining oil, the onion, and the green chili. Cook 5 minutes, until the onion softens.
Stir in the garlic, the ginger, the cumin, the turmeric, and the salt. Cook 1 minute.
Add the tomato and cook 3 minutes, until it breaks down.
Add the spinach in handfuls, letting each batch wilt. Cook about 8 minutes, until the leaves are soft and the pan is not watery.
Stir in the garam masala, the cream, and the paneer. Simmer 3 minutes, until the paneer is hot and the sauce is thick and green.

attribution.note: No saag paneer or palak paneer page. Matar Paneer is peas, not spinach.

name: Mexican Street Corn Salad
steps: Husk the corn. Chop the cilantro and crumble the cotija cheese. Cut the lime in half.
Brush the corn with the oil. Heat a grill or a dry skillet over high heat.
Cook the corn, turning, until the kernels are charred in spots and hot through, about 8 minutes.
Cool the ears 2 minutes, then cut the kernels off the cobs into a bowl.
Stir in the mayonnaise, the chili powder, the salt, and the juice of the lime.
Fold in the cotija cheese and the cilantro.
The salad is done when the kernels are coated and still a little warm. Serve it that way.

attribution.note: No elote, esquites, or Mexican street-corn page.
